canonical_data: A local SQLite database at `~/.engram/engram.db` holding observations, sessions, prompts, and relations, with FTS5 indexes beside them
current_repo_note: Installed and health-probed by the published Gentle-AI workflow command line, but a separate operational boundary: its own repository, releases, and install path, and agent-agnostic by design.
strengths: One agent-agnostic store reachable four ways — MCP tools, an HTTP API, a command line, and a terminal UI — so the same memory serves whichever coding agent a developer runs
Local SQLite is authoritative and the documentation says so plainly, with cloud features scoped to optional replication and shared access

Memory management is modelled rather than left to the model: duplicate counts, revision counts on a shared topic key, a supersession chain between entries, soft deletion, and review-and-expiry columns
weaknesses: Retrieval is lexical only: FTS5 with bm25 plus pinned, recency, and stability boosts, while the embedding columns in the schema are a reservation no query uses
Current releases are pre-1.0 candidates, so the interface a deployer builds against is still moving
Cloud replication and shared access are the project's own service, so using them moves the boundary off the local database the rest of the design protects
why_it_matters: Shows an agent's long-term memory can be an ordinary local database a person can read, edit, export, and re-import, rather than a hosted service the agent alone can reach.
